newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kumar brothers charged for bribery in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Kumar brothers charged for bribery in Singapore.

text.p: Flamboyant entreprenuerial brothers Raj and Ashok Kumar have been charged in a Singapore court with bribery, The Straits Times reported on Thursday.

They were charged with offering at least Singapore $1 million (US$700,000) to a bank manager to lower the annual interest rate of company bonds used to re-finance hotels they partly owned in Australia and New Zealand.
The pair wanted the interest rate of company bonds halved from 10 and 12 percent to between five and six percent, the newspaper said.
It said the bribe was offered to Chia Kin Hon, general manager of HL Bank, the Singapore branch of Malaysia's Heong Leong Bank, on May 9, 1995. The hotels were sold in December last year.
The bank said in a statement it had not raised any bonds for the brothers and that the alleged offer was a private matter between Chia and the Kumars, the newspaper said.
Both brothers have opted for trial. Bail was set at S$1 million each.
If found guilty, they face a fine of up to S$100,000, or five years in jail, or both.
A pre-trial conference was set for July 2.
Lawyers acting for the brothers were not immediately available for comment.
